subject: SLA remedies and escrowed fee request — proposed liability triggers
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <j.miles@horizonhealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Health Legal <legal@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Contract: Remedies for repeated SLA breaches

Dylan —

Thanks for the continuing conversation. Our legal team has reviewed the SLA language and we need to push on concrete remedies beyond service credits for repeat severe outages. Specifically, Horizon Health is asking for the following redlines: 

- Fee-at-risk: 10% of the contracted ARR for the first year to be held in escrow and released only if SLA thresholds are met; payout to customer in the event of material failure.
- Termination right: ability to terminate for convenience with pro-rated refund of prepaid fees if we experience two Severity-1 incidents within a rolling 90-day window.
- Liquidated damages: $5,000 per full day of continuous outage beyond the first 24 hours for Severity-1 events.

We understand Redwood's position on liability caps, but given the regulatory sensitivity of our workload, these items are non-negotiable on our side without equivalent contractual safeguards (fee at risk and termination).

I've attached our redline to the most recent SOW. Can you get us a written position from Redwood legal and ops by COB Monday? If you prefer, we can hop on a 30-min call to walk through specifics.

Best,
Jordan Miles
Dir., Cloud Security & Ops
Horizon Health

Attachment: Horizon_SLA_redlines_v1.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Horizon Health redlines — need negotiation strategy

Team — forwarding Horizon's redlines (see attachment). Key asks: escrowed fee (10%), termination after two S1s in 90 days, and per-day liquidated damages. Our high-level take: credits only is our standard; liquidation and termination for brief outages expose us to open liability and churn risk.

Proposed Redwood counter (draft):
- Service-credit schedule tied to measured availability (retain standard cap at 12 months of fees).
- Escrow alternative: Redwood will accept a one-time "stability deposit" equal to 6% of first-year committed fees, held in escrow for the first contract year only; deposit converts to credits for measured breaches per the SLA schedule, and is refundable pro-rata otherwise.
- Termination carve: customer may terminate only for prolonged, unremediated outages defined as either (a) a continuous outage > 48 hours OR (b) two S1 incidents within 120 days where Redwood failed to implement mutually agreed remediation and prevention plan.
- No per-day liquidated damages; instead, a headline cap and expedited remediation obligations plus a dedicated technical account manager and monthly operational review.

Questions: 1) Legal — is the stability deposit an acceptable compromise vs. 10% escrow? 2) Infra (Karthik) — can we commit to the 48-hour continuous outage threshold and joint incident review? 3) CS (Lauren) — does this meet Horizon’s risk needs from an account-management standpoint or will it sink the deal?

Attaching a draft counter redline for quick review: Redwood_SLA_counter_redline.pdf

—Dylan

From: markus_klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Horizon Health redlines — need negotiation strategy

Dylan —

Quick notes from legal: the "stability deposit" approach is a workable commercial compromise provided we: (1) limit exposure to direct damages only, (2) set an absolute liability cap equal to the greater of 100% of fees paid in the prior 12 months or the deposit amount (whichever is greater), and (3) expressly exclude consequential and regulatory fines from recoverable liquid sums. We should also add language making escrow release contingent upon mutually-accepted incident verification.

From infra (cc Karthik): the 48-hour continuous outage commitment is borderline but achievable with our current fallbacks (regional failover + burst capacity). Karthik suggests the 120-day window for multiple S1s is safer than 90 days and gives us time to remediate.

Lauren — please confirm whether adding a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) and monthly SLA reports will calm the customer enough to accept the deposit vs. full escrow.

If everyone signs off, I recommend we present the counter precisely as bullets (deposit %, termination triggers, verification/process) and avoid any numeric per-day liquidated damages language — that is a hard no from legal.

-Markus

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <j.miles@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 23 Mar 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood counterproposal re: SLA remedies (stability deposit + operational commitments)

Jordan —

Appreciate the patience while we reviewed this internally. Below is Redwood's written counterproposal. We think it addresses Horizon's operational risk while keeping the contract sustainable for both sides.

Summary (counterproposal):
1) Stability deposit: Redwood will accept a one-time stability deposit equal to 6% of the first-year committed fees, held in escrow for Year 1 only. The deposit is refundable pro-rata if SLA thresholds are met; otherwise it converts to service credits per the SLA schedule.
2) Termination triggers: Horizon may terminate the Agreement for material service failure only in either of these cases: (a) a single continuous outage exceeding 48 hours; or (b) two Severity-1 incidents within a rolling 120-day window where Redwood failed to implement a mutually-agreed remediation plan within 10 business days.
3) Liquidated damages: Redwood cannot accept per-day liquidated damages. In lieu of daily damages, we propose expedited remediation, a dedicated TAM, prioritized capacity for Horizon's production workload, and monthly SLA reporting with joint incident verification.
4) Verification & release: escrow release or credit conversion will be subject to joint verification by Horizon and Redwood with agreed-upon telemetry and incident logs.

Next steps: I've attached our redline (Redwood_SLA_counter_redline.pdf) and included a DocuSign link to a limited amendment if you want to move quickly: https://www.docusign.com/recipient?envelopeId=abc-123-hrz. If Horizon is comfortable in principle, let's schedule a 30-min call to lock the remaining language — I have availability Thu 3/24 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 3/25 13:00–14:00 PT.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_counter_redline.pdf

Subject: Re: Redwood counterproposal re: SLA remedies (stability deposit + operational commitments)

Dylan —

Thanks for the thoughtful counter — the stability deposit and the 120-day window look reasonable as written. Our legal team still wants minimal escrow language tweaks around verification timing, but we can take those as redline edits rather than reopening economics.

We'd like the TAM commitment formalized in the SOW and a 3-month pilot period for the deposit model (after which we re-evaluate). Can we accept the DocuSign envelope and then push a short redline for verification? I can have our counsel send the tweaks by EOD Thursday.

Let’s take the call Friday 3/25 at 13:00 PT.

-Jordan
